rows.question: Continue with your compilable kernel and host launch. Explain precisely what threads 70 through 95 do in the original kernel and why successful launch checks do not establish correctness. In your replacement, prove that every shared-memory value read by thread zero was initialized, and identify which thread writes the output when valid is zero. Keep the launch at one block of 96 threads for every valid value, including zero; do not handle zero by skipping the kernel or initializing the output on the host.
rows.recognizedQuestion: Explain precisely what Thread Seventy through Ninety Five do in the original kernel and why successful launch checks do not establish correctness In your replacement prove that every shared memory value read by thread zero was initialized and identify which thread writes the output when valid is zero Keep the launch at one block of ninety six threads for every valid value including zero do not handle zero by skipping the kernel or initializing the output on the host
rows.answer:
In the original kernel with valid = 70, threads 70–95 evaluate `threadIdx.x < valid` as false. They skip the entire conditional—including the input load, shared-memory store, `__syncthreads()`, and summation—and then finish if there is no further code. Threads 0–69 enter the conditional and encounter the barrier. A block barrier inside a conditional requires that condition to be uniform across the block; this nonuniform condition violates that contract. The behavior is undefined, not a guarantee that every device hangs.

Successful immediate launch checks establish neither completed execution nor synchronization correctness. The kernel executes asynchronously, so a launch can be accepted without those checks detecting the divergent barrier. A responsive host endpoint likewise does not prove that the GPU stream has completed.

In the replacement, keep `sum_valid<<<1, 96, 0, stream>>>(device_input, device_output, valid)` for every valid value from 0 through 96. For each shared-memory value `values[i]` read by thread zero, the loop guarantees `0 <= i < valid <= 96`. Thread `i` therefore exists, passes the load condition, and initializes `values[i]` from `input[i]` before the unconditional barrier. All 96 threads reach that barrier, which orders those writes and makes them visible to thread zero before its reads; no uninitialized shared entries are read.

When valid is zero, all 96 threads skip the input loads but still execute the barrier. Thread zero initializes its local sum to `0.0f`, executes zero loop iterations, and writes `0.0f` to the output. The kernel is not skipped, and the host does not initialize the output.
